preparation: Supply the actual selected source paragraphs with publisher/date/place and the original diagram/table. Use a verified Canada locator to distinguish Ottawa, Toronto and the particular community programme places; do not use a territory map to imply exclusive legal boundaries.

For the whole feature claim, retain actual learner-local natural, managed and built examples and positional map description, with adult-verified resources. For the whole visual claim, read the table/diagram alongside the texts, explain what each adds, and make a supported synthesis.

For the actual added-information visual check, give Source A as the selected NCC operator text about weather-dependent operation, and Source B as the original comparison table of the three particular cases. The table adds distinct Toronto care and NFN/community-language examples not in that operator text. Explain the added case breadth, then combine the operational qualification from A with the diverse features in B to conclude that winter recreation is a conditional, selected part of a more varied representation. Neither the operator text alone nor the table alone supplies that complete conclusion. Keep the source facts attached; this is an original evidence organizer, not a national-opinion dataset.
actions: Identify the actual physical, built and social features across these cases. Explain how the skating setting depends both on physical conditions and human management; a built canal is not an untouched natural river.

Interpret the diagram and comparison table. Combine the promotional representation with the operator’s weather qualification: explain how a selected feature can contribute to a winter-capital image without proving year-round availability or every resident’s self-identity.

Assess the contribution of each selected feature to a Canadian public image using stated criteria: actual supporting detail, people/places it includes, and what it omits. Compare winter recreation with actual community care and continuing language/knowledge transmission; none is a complete portrait of Canada.

Use the actual Nipissing First Nation language account as a community-authoritative social-feature case: explain how its stated language priority, fluent-speaker learning and community communication support the Nation’s expressed cultural continuity/identity. Ground the explanation in its particular words and programmes. Compare this community account with the operator/tourism winter-capital image: whose identity, purpose and audience are represented in each? A programme description does not prove every member feels alike or that measured revival has occurred. Retain distinct Métis and Inuit cases in the full renewal check rather than present NFN as all Indigenous peoples.

Produce an original short account: select two or more complementary features, explain their image/identity contribution and revise a universal stereotype. Attribute each representation and distinguish fact, a supported interpretation and an unsupported population-wide statement.
protocol.positive: Explains and assesses supported physical/built/social feature→selected public-image relationships AND the particular source-supported social-feature→community-identity relationship, retaining attribution/variation limits and actual text/visual synthesis.
nearMisses: Labels an attractive feature without explaining its image contribution.
Calls all Canadians skaters or assumes one community programme proves every member’s identity.
Replaces actual source facts with a personal self-map, or says a promotional claim proves a measured nationwide opinion.
Assesses only how visitors see Canada but never explains the selected community’s own source-supported identity relationship.
